description: server.js's `wss.on('connection', ...)` handler (server.js:356-455, ~100 lines) mixes network I/O (raw WebSocket wiring) with a non-trivial STATE MACHINE (openGeminiLive/onGeminiEnd reconnect logic with mutable geminiReconnects/gotAudio/liveWsOpened counters) inline in a single closure, with no seam for unit testing. This is inconsistent with the project's OWN established pattern in this exact feature: routeTelnyxMessage/routeGeminiMessage were deliberately extracted to lib/call-bridge.cjs specifically so they could be exercised by fake-socket unit tests (call-bridge.cjs:36 comment: 'Pure routing core (testable with a fake socket)'). The reconnect decision logic (whether to retry vs. give up, given gotAudio + geminiReconnects + carrier state) is exactly the kind of pure decision that could have been extracted as a testable function (e.g. `decideReconnect({gotAudio, reconnects, carrierOpen}) -> 'retry'|'give-up'`) the same way routeGeminiMessage was. Leaving it inline is precisely why FIND-001 (a real bug) and FIND-002 (zero test coverage of that bug) exist — untestable code hid a broken invariant. Per project coding-style.md ('MANY SMALL FILES > FEW LARGE FILES... Extract utilities from large components'), this is a structural violation, not merely a style nit.

evidence.snippet: wss.on("connection", (carrierWs, req) => { ... let gemini = null; let liveWsOpened = 0; let gotAudio = false; let geminiReconnects = 0; ... function openGeminiLive() { ... const onGeminiEnd = (reason) => { ... }; ... } ... });
